chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who owed a portion of fasting from the month of Ramadan, then the next Ramadan caught him (before he paid it off). He said: 'If he was healthy in between, but did not pay it off until the next Ramadan caught him, then he must fast and feed one poor person for each day. And if he was sick in between until the next Ramadan caught him, then there is no obligation upon him except fasting, if he is healthy. But if the illness persisted upon him, then he must feed one poor person for each day.'

key_terms.طَائِفَةٌ: A portion or part (of the missed fasts)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who misses Ramadan fasts and does not make them up until the next Ramadan arrives?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between temporary illness and chronic incapacity regarding the expiation (*kaffarah*) for delayed *qada* of Ramadan fasts. It establishes that mere delay due to health issues does not incur feeding the poor unless the illness persists until the next Ramadan, a nuance critical in Shia fiqh for determining the obligation of *fidya* alongside *qada*.
